requirements_summary: Workload: multi-turn chat/agent with tool calling (external API pulls, SQL lookups)
Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end (prompt + first byte streaming) <= 500ms for 512-token exchanges; prefer <400ms
Streaming: sub-100ms chunk latency for first response segments desirable
Throughput: 100-300 concurrent sessions typical; burst to 800 during peak
Cost sensitivity: moderate — prioritize consistent latency over cheapest token price
Model preferences: flexible - open model variants acceptable; want smaller fast models for routine routing and larger models as fallback
Routing needs: region-aware routing (NA), fallback to alternate model/region on overload
Compliance: SSO/SAML, audit logs for queries, KMS-integrated key management, data retention controls
migration_notes: Currently on IncumbentAI; recent model update caused 2x-3x latency spikes during peak hours - engineering quote: 'felt 2-3x slower, lots of streaming stalls'
Primary migration driver: unreliable streaming and opaque fallback behavior from incumbent
Procurement: sticky due to 6-month early termination penalty on incumbent contract
Engineering: small adapter already written; wants a runbook for canary cutover and fallback to incumbent while validation runs

benchmarking_summary: POC methodology: 2-week parallel run, traffic mirrored 20% to Redwood Hosted API and 80% to incumbent; identical prompt sets (~10k requests), session affinity preserved for cache benefits
Key metrics (interim 2/22-3/1): Redwood streaming p50 140ms, p95 360ms; incumbent p50 320ms, p95 780ms (measured end-to-end to first token chunk)
Observations: Redwood showed more stable KV cache warmup behavior across sessions; incumbent had sporadic stalls tied to model version rollouts
Functional: tool calling reliability higher on Redwood in test (fewer retries), streaming chunks arrived more regularly enabling smoother client UX
Open items: full cost per unit token at production QPS, Dedicated throughput guarantees, formal SLA language for streaming p95
